title: Eventual coordinate surjectivity on twisted sections
statement: Let k be a field and P=Proj k[x_0,x_1] as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. For a coherent O_P-module G [pqf-def-coherent], there is an integer N>=0 such that for every z>=N and every section s of G tensor O_P(z+1), there are sections s0,s1 of G tensor O_P(z) with s=x0*s0+x1*s1. Multiplication is the map G whiskered with twistMul of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. No finiteness assertion about sections or their direct sum is made.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 01YS (4); coordinate split exact sequence on P1, checked on D+(x0) and D+(x1); online source read because local checkout is absent

proof.text: Use coordinate multiplication to form 0 -> O(-1) -> O^2 -> O(1) -> 0, with maps t -> (-x1*t,x0*t) and (a,b) -> x0*a+x1*b. On D+(xi), xi is a unit in the trivialized twists, so the sequence is split exact. Tensor with G tensor O(z); local splitting preserves exactness without assuming G flat. Twist addition identifies the kernel with G tensor O(z-1). The quotient maps are exactly G whiskered with twistMul by x0 and x1, by the fraction formula.

Identify the Proj twists with the twists on the standard projective line using the chart isomorphism and uniqueness of TwistData. Coherence on projective space over a field supplies the quasi-coherence and finite presentation required by Serre vanishing. Apply vanishing to G and choose a natural bound N such that H1(G tensor O(z-1)) is zero for z>=N.

The long exact sequence makes the section map from two copies of Gamma(G tensor O(z)) onto Gamma(G tensor O(z+1)) surjective. Sections commute with finite direct sums; read a preimage as a pair to obtain the displayed sum. The zero sheaf case uses the zero pair.
